subject: GDPR: DPA template request + SCC module preference & next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Bueno <maria.bueno@finovest.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:12:00+00:00
Subject: Quick follow-up from today's compliance sync + DPA ask

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay synchronized: 

1) GDPR roles: you indicated Finovest will act as Controller for customer data and would like Redwood to act as Processor for telemetry and inference-related logs. Please confirm if that is still accurate.

2) DPA: could you share any DPA template or preferred language you need us to use? We can share our standard DPA if that speeds review.

3) SCC modules: you flagged a preference for SCC modular approach to handle restricted transfer clauses — do you prefer the controller-to-controller or processor-focused module set? If you don’t have a strong preference, we typically propose the Processor Addendum + Module 2 (for restricted transfers) for our hosted offering.

4) Evidence: you asked about SOC 2 status and data flow diagrams. We have a SOC 2 Type II report for 2026 Q2 (I attached a stub) and can pull a redacted data flow diagram for the services in scope.

Next steps proposed from Redwood: we will send a draft DPA and point to the SCC module we recommend, and attach the vendor security questionnaire you requested. If Finovest can share a DPA template or markups, we’ll prioritize that.

Attachments: Finovest_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (please complete the sections marked "security for hosted inference"), SOC2_Report_RW_2026Q2.pdf (redacted).

Can you confirm the controller/processor mapping and whether you want us to start from your DPA or ours?

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Maria Bueno <maria.bueno@finovest.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Finovest Legal Team <legal@finovest.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up from today's compliance sync + DPA ask

Hi Sergio —

Thanks for the clear notes and the attachments. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Controller/Processor: yes — Finovest is Controller for customer personal data. We expect Redwood to be Processor for any data ingested via the API. We also need clarity on any downstream subprocessors (hosting providers, analytics).

- DPA: we prefer to start from our template where possible. I attached a short checklist of clauses we usually require; I'll send the full DPA template once legal completes a quick internal review.

- SCC modules: Finovest legal favors the modular SCC approach. For a Processor scenario we typically require Module 1 (Processor to Controller) + Module 2 (restricted transfer safeguards). If Redwood has strong technical controls for restricted transfers, we may accept Module 2 with certain addenda.

- Evidence: we will need the SOC 2 Type II report and a service boundary description. Also request: encryption-at-rest details and key management (do you support customer-managed keys / KMS?)

Action items for Redwood (from Finovest):
- Share Redwood's standard DPA (or a redline-friendly version).
- Confirm subprocessors and where data is hosted (region).
- Provide SOC 2 PDF and a short data flow diagram.

I'll follow up with our DPA template by tomorrow EOD.

Regards,
Maria Bueno
Senior Counsel, Finovest
maria.bueno@finovest.com
[Attachment: Finovest_DPA_Checklist.pdf]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>

Folks — forwarding Finovest's reply and checklist (see above). Key asks from them: 1) they prefer to start from their DPA, 2) want SCC Module 1+2 for Processor scenario, 3) SOC2, service boundary, KMS details, 4) subprocessors list.

Can legal ops/privsec confirm:
- Is our standard approach for Processor customers to propose the Processor Addendum + Module 2 enough, or should we proactively propose both Module 1+2 redlines when a prospect requests it?
- Do we have a current subprocessors list and a short statement on KMS/customer-managed keys?

I attached: redwood_dpa_draft_v1.docx and the questionnaire we asked Finovest to fill. If you can propose language we can send back to Maria that aligns with our security posture, I’ll get it out today.

Thanks — Sergio

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-28T17:03:00+00:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Quick follow-up from today's compliance sync + DPA ask

Sergio / team —

Quick guidance after reviewing their checklist and our draft DPA: 

1) Controller/Processor mapping: accept Finovest's framing (Controller = Finovest; Processor = Redwood). We'll add a short subprocessors clause with a recent list and commit to 30-day notice for new subprocessors.

2) SCC modules: recommend offering a Processor-focused pathway. Practical path: send our draft DPA plus a Processor Addendum that references SCC Module 2 as the primary restricted-transfer module. If Finovest insists on Module 1 language, provide a short redline that maps Module 1 obligations into Processor context — explain technical limits (e.g., we cannot accept Controller-to-Controller transfers obligations).

3) Evidence & KMS: attach SOC2_Report_RW_2026Q2.pdf (redacted) and provide KMS options: (a) default platform-managed keys (AES-256) hosted in EU regions, (b) enterprise customers can opt for customer-managed keys via AWS KMS or Google Cloud KMS (we have an integration playbook).

4) Next steps to keep deal momentum: 
- Sergio: reply to Maria confirming controller/processor mapping and say we will start from Finovest's DPA but share our redline-friendly draft in parallel. Attach SOC2 and a short service boundary summary (I included a one-pager we can send).
- Neha: prepare subprocessors list and a short statement on data residency for EU accounts.
- Karthik: prepare a brief note on our KMS integrations and sample config guide.

I'll draft suggested wording and upload to the shared Drive link (send to Maria as a single reply thread). We should aim to close redline loop within 5 business days to avoid slowing procurement.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Operations, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
